title: Deal or Handle?
lede: In Portuguese, both are “lidar com”. In English, the context decides. Look at real examples, find the contexts, and make the rule yourself.

options.t: I don't know handle with it.
options.msg: You chose “I don't know handle with it.” Now you know why it is wrong: handle never takes “with”, and “não sei” here means can't. Say “I can't deal with it” or “I can't handle it.”
You chose “I can't deal with it.” Correct! Use it when the problem is about feelings or a difficult person: “My ex keeps calling me. I can't deal with it.”
You chose “I can't handle it.” Correct! Use it when it is about capacity, when something is too much for you: “Three jobs? I can't handle it.”

warmup.close: Both B and C are correct. The context decides. Now tell a partner one thing you can handle easily and one thing that is hard for you to deal with.

notice.q: Show “deal”. When deal is a verb, what word comes right after it?
notice.ok: Yes! The verb is always deal with + something.
notice.no: Look again. Sort by “next word” to help you.

opts.t: the thing directly: it, the pressure, the money

notice.ok: Right! handle + it / the pressure. No “with”. (In “handle the glasses with care”, with goes with care.)
notice.no: Look again. Do you see “handle with the problem”?

notice.q: Show “deal”. Look at the words after “deal with”: the emails, the broken window, stress, sadness, my neighbor. These are…

opts.t: tasks, problems, feelings and people you need to face

notice.ok: Exactly. We deal with things that need our attention, and often they are difficult or unpleasant.
notice.no: Not quite. Are emails, sadness and a rude neighbor nice things?

notice.q: Show “handle”. Look at the words around it: can, couldn't, too much, well, badly. What do they tell us?

opts.t: handle is about capacity: can you manage it? how well?

notice.ok: Yes! handle often talks about capacity and performance: I can handle it, she handled it well.
notice.no: Look at can / couldn't / too much / well / badly again. What do these words measure?

notice.q: Show “deal”. Find “it's a deal” and “no big deal”. Here, deal is…

opts.t: a noun: an agreement, or something important

notice.ok: Right. It's a deal! = combinado. No big deal = nada demais.
notice.no: There is no “with” here, and there is “a” before deal. What does that tell you?

classify.title: Four contexts
classify.task: Read each sentence. What is the situation? Tap a context.

groups.title: A task or a problem
groups.desc: You do something about it, now or later.

groups.title: Capacity
groups.desc: Can I manage it? How well did I do it?

groups.title: In charge, or hands
groups.desc: Your job or role, or you touch it.

items.s: How do you <mark>deal with</mark> stress before an exam?
Don't worry about the project. I can <mark>handle</mark> it.
In our family, my mom <mark>handles</mark> the money.
I can't <mark>deal with</mark> my neighbor. He's so rude!
Who's going to <mark>deal with</mark> the broken window?
She <mark>handled</mark> the angry customer really well.
Wash your hands before you <mark>handle</mark> food.
He couldn't <mark>handle</mark> the pressure, so he quit.
Nurses <mark>deal with</mark> sick and scared people every day.

after.q: Now look at your four groups. Which verb do you see in each one?

opts.t: Task and Feelings → handle · Capacity and In charge → deal with
Task and Feelings → deal with · Capacity and In charge → handle
All four groups use both verbs

after.ok: Yes! The context helps you choose: tasks, feelings and difficult people → deal with. Capacity, being in charge, hands → handle.
after.no: Look at the underlined words in each group again.

lines.pre: After the verb deal, we need
For a task, a problem, a feeling or a difficult person, we usually use
For capacity (I can / can't, too much) or how well someone did something, we usually use
For your job or role, or for touching something with your hands, we use

boxes.ex: I'll deal with the emails tomorrow.
How do you deal with stress? I can't deal with him!
I can handle it. She handled it really well.
boxes.pt: Dar conta, ter controle, se sair bem.

boxes.ex: My mom handles the money. Handle with care.

rule.both: Sometimes both are possible“deal with a problem” and “handle a problem” are both correct. The focus is different:deal with = you face it and do something about it.handle = you manage it, you are in control.
rule.never: Never: <s>handle with the problem</s> <s>deal the problem</s>
rule.hint: deal is also a noun: It's a deal! (combinado) · no big deal (nada demais) · a good deal (um bom negócio).

situations.c: Your boss gives you a big project. You feel confident.
You have 40 unread emails, but you are having lunch.
situations.why: A task you will do something about later → deal with.

situations.c: Your friend's grandmother died last week.
situations.s: “She's ___ a lot of sadness right now.”

situations.c: A waiter talks about his job at a restaurant.
situations.s: “At the end of the night, I ___ the money.”
situations.why: His role, he is in charge of it → handle.

situations.c: A manager talks to an employee after a difficult meeting.
situations.why: How well someone did it → handled … well. (“dealt” is wrong here: it needs “with”.)

situations.c: Your roommate never cleans and plays loud music at 3 a.m.
situations.why: A difficult person you have to put up with → I can't deal with him.

situations.c: A sign on a box in the post office.
situations.why: Touching something with your hands → Handle with care.

situations.c: Your new job has long hours and a lot of pressure. You are tired.
situations.why: Capacity → too much to handle. (“too much to deal with” is OK too, but never “too much to deal”.)

textsTip: Tip: is there a “with” after the gap? Is it about a task, feelings, capacity or being in charge?

texts.ctx: Rafa started a job in a busy shop. His friend Jen calls him.
turns: How's the new job? Is it too much to [[handle]]?
No, I can [[handle]] it. But every day I have to [[deal with]] angry customers.
That sounds hard. Who [[handles]] the money in the shop?
My manager. Yesterday a customer shouted at me, and I [[handled]] it really well!
Nice! If there's a big problem, call me. I'll help you [[deal with]] it.

texts.ctx: Leo and Mia are students. They have exams next week.
turns: Three exams next week. I can't [[handle]] all this pressure!
Relax, it's no big [[deal]]. How do you usually [[deal with]] stress?
I play video games… for six hours.
Ha! That's not a good way to [[deal with/handle]] it. Let's make a study plan.
OK. You help me study, I buy the pizza. [[Deal]]?

texts.ctx: Ana writes a blog post about moving to another country.
texts.prose: Moving to Canada was hard. In the first month, I had to [[deal with]] a lot of loneliness. My English was OK, so I could [[handle]] simple conversations, but phone calls were too much to [[handle]]. I also had to [[deal with]] a difficult landlord who never answered my messages. Now, after one year, I think I [[handled/dealt with]] the change pretty well!

errors.s: I need to handle with this problem.
errors.fix: I need to handle this problem. / I need to deal with this problem.
errors.why: handle never takes “with” before the thing.

errors.s: How do you deal with stress?

errors.fix: I can't deal with this situation. / I can't handle this situation.

errors.s: Don't worry, I can handle it.
She handles with the money in our company.
errors.fix: She handles the money in our company.
errors.why: In charge → handle + the thing, no “with”.
For the topic of a book or movie, we say deal with.

errors.s: Wash your hands before you deal with food.
errors.fix: Wash your hands before you handle food.

errors.s: Be careful! Handle the box with care.

errors.fix: It's too much to handle. / It's too much to deal with.
errors.why: deal alone does not work here. Use handle, or deal with.

steps: Type deal with. Which words come after it? Write three. Are they nice things or difficult things?
Type handle and click Word sketch. Look at the words used with it. Do you see well, badly, pressure, situation?
Type handled well. Who handled what? Write two examples.
Type handle with. What word comes after with?
Write three sentences about you: something you can handle easily, something that is hard to deal with, and something you handled well.
